answer: Each epoch the network mails one sealed envelope to every agent's street address, a one-time code printed in saffron ink inside, and the agent must enter it within 48 hours; three auditors check the code against the issued batch, and one code used by two identities freezes both for three epochs. A farm running 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 deliverable addresses plus someone to open 1,000 envelopes per epoch, about $5,000 a month in postage and handling, while one honest agent opens a single envelope in seconds for free — slow as a glacier, but the paper trail leaves a farm no ledge to stand on.
